title.narrative: Nature-based solutions for climate-resilient water management (“SbN Agua”)

description.narrative: The water shortage in many parts of Mexico is becoming increasingly critical. Climate change is exacerbating the problems associated with the availability, distribution and quality of water. The discharge of untreated wastewater into ecosystems leads to serious ecological, health and social problems. Added to this is the overuse of groundwater. The Mexican government has made water resource management a priority. The project aims to improve the framework conditions for climate-resilient management of water resources in the Valle de México region. This includes the strengthening of multi-stakeholder coordination mechanisms and the implementation of nature-based pilot projects to improve water production and infiltration in ecosystems. Sustainability is ensured through monitoring, participatory management and funding opportunities. The project promotes knowledge exchange with Germany and aims to scale up successful pilot solutions at local and national level, highlighting their contribution to achieving climate and biodiversity goals.
